title: Prediction Standards report envelope
description: The document `predictions check|audit|explain|status --json` writes to stdout. This file IS the definition of "documented key" that ADR 0011 rests on: a consumer holding schemaVersion M.m.p may assume every key documented at the same major and any minor at or below m is present with the documented type and meaning, and may assume nothing about the absence of other keys. `additionalProperties` is false at the two levels this contract covers — the top-level document and the entries of `records[]` — because a schema that admits undocumented keys cannot serve as a definition of which keys are documented. Below those two levels the contract stops, deliberately and visibly: `parameters` is defined by project-policy.schema.json, and `records[].results[]` items are the rule catalog's surface rather than the envelope's. Those are typed here and not enumerated, and ADR 0011's bump table therefore does not govern them. `predictions policy --json` is NOT this document; it has a disjoint `status` vocabulary (ok/findings/invalid) and no contract of its own.

schemaVersion.description: The report envelope version, independent of the standards version, the prediction-record schema version and the adapter schemaVersion. Four streams; a move in one says nothing about the others.

command.description: Which subcommand produced this report. Deliberately not an enum: ADR 0011 D7 declares this value set OPEN, so a future subcommand emitting this envelope is a minor change, and a consumer was never entitled to enumerate it.

policy.description: The project policy this report was evaluated under, relative to the invocation, or null when none was found.

asOf.description: The instant every staleness and expiry comparison ran against. A verdict is valid as of an instant, not as of a commit.

status.description: The single authoritative disposition over the checked set (ADR 0010). Present exactly when `command` is "check"; `audit`, `explain` and `status` reach no verdict by design. That conditional presence is asserted by a test rather than by a `oneOf` discriminated on `command` — ADR 0008 part 2's reasoning, applied per command instead of per version: a branch per variant duplicates the whole shape, and the copies drift. The value set is CLOSED (ADR 0011 D7); adding a sixth member is a major change, because StandardsEnforcer fails closed on a status its adapter does not declare.

records.description: One entry per record found under the target, in the order they were loaded.

aggregate.description: How many records landed in each disposition. Not the verdict: `aggregate` and `status` answer different questions, and neither substitutes for the other.

parameters.description: The thresholds this evaluation ran under, published because a verdict depending on a materiality threshold nobody can see is a verdict nobody can check. Its keys are defined by schemas/project-policy.schema.json, which is where a policy author is governed; enumerating them a second time here would be two definitions of one thing.

record.description: One record's outcome. Three keys are always present, whatever happened to the file. The remaining fourteen come from the per-record envelope and are present exactly when `parseError` is null — a record that could not be read produced no envelope, and still produced a status. That conditional presence is asserted by a test rather than by a `oneOf`, for the same reason as the top-level `status`.

file.description: The record's path relative to the invocation.

parseError.description: Why the record could not be read, or null when it was read. Never a verdict: an unreadable record is NOT_EVALUATED, which is the absence of a finding rather than a mild one.

status.description: This record's disposition. Always present since ADR 0010 — before it, a parse-error entry carried no status at all, and that change is half of why the envelope earned a minor bump.

schemaVersion.description: The same envelope version as the enclosing report, and the same contract. One version written in two places is two versions, so both emitters read one constant.

record.description: The record's declared id, or null when it declared none.

score.description: Percentage of scored rules that passed, or null when nothing was scored. Never a proxy for the status.

assurance.description: How each applicable rule was established. A rule nothing evaluated is counted in `notEvaluated`, never as a pass — the oldest commitment in this pack, and the reason SUPPORTED does not imply every applicable rule passed.

blockedBy.description: The rule ids of the non-exemptible failures that blocked this record. Empty when none did.

denominator.description: What the score was computed over, published so the score can be checked rather than trusted.

frameworkCoverage.description: Framework maturity: how much of the framework has been turned into evaluated rules. Never how well supported this prediction is. Combining the two would let a coverage improvement look like a support improvement.

results.description: One entry per rule considered. WHERE THIS CONTRACT STOPS. The entries are typed and not enumerated, so ADR 0011's promise and its bump table do not reach inside them: a result entry's keys follow the rule catalog, which moves on the standards' cycle rather than the envelope's, and a schema claiming otherwise would either freeze the catalog or quietly lie. A consumer needing per-rule detail is reading an unversioned surface and should be told so — see docs/json-output.md.
